title: Presentation Builder fork: grounded CRM deck + citation-metagraph skill
one_liner: Fork of an HTML deck factory, extended with an evidence-graph method where every slide number carries a claim id traced to source, locator and quote; worked case: a 27-slide CRM scenario deck.
purpose: Upstream is a Claude Code deck factory: a script in scripts/ plus a style reference become one self-contained HTML presentation under design rules in Claude.MD. The owner's added work turns it into a grounded-presentation pipeline. For the executive deck 'Three stories, three scenarios' (WISeKey group CRM, HubSpot portal [id]) a multi-agent workflow explored six source families, ranked what was built (keep / simplify / consolidate / pay for), built an evidence metagraph, attacked every claim with two verification lenses, then rendered the deck from the graph so each number carries data-claim and data-source. It deliberately presents three scenarios (DIY, DIY + partner, HubSpot-native) without recommending one: a presentation layer, not a decision layer. The method was distilled into the reusable skill structured-citation-metagraph with two stdlib guard scripts, and a second producer converts the HTML deck to Markdown and then PowerPoint. A sequel on 2026-10-12 appended three remediation-plan slides (layers L1-L3).
domain: Evidence-grounded presentation generation (LLM multi-agent tooling, CRM audit)
stack: Claude Code workflow script (agent / parallel / phase)
HubSpot MCP read-only HubSQL (as a source)

entry_points.command: Create a new presentation using @scripts/your-script.txt in the style of @style-references/your-chosen-style.html
entry_points.what: Upstream usage: a Claude Code prompt that turns a script into a single HTML deck saved in Finished Presentations/, following Claude.MD.

Run from the skill folder (a copy also sits in projects/crm-three-scenarios/). Scores co-cited node pairs, rewrites metagraph.md idempotently, and exits 2 if any planned view cites an ungrounded node (the presentation-layer guard).
Prints the top-N neighbours of every node with combined / co / prox values, writes nothing, still runs the guard.

Skill script (.claude/skills/structured-citation-metagraph/scripts/). Checks the built deck against the graph: unknown, non-fact or refuted claim ids exit 1; --strict also fails on ids no view planned; lists every caveated claim.
Opens the deck in headless Chromium at 1920x1080 @2x, exhausts each slide's animations, screenshots every inline SVG of at least 200x80 px to slideNN-figK.png and writes manifest.json.
Parses the HTML deck into pandoc slide-show Markdown (crm-three-scenarios.md), chunked by an 11-line budget; --pptx also runs pandoc with the 16 pt reference template.

entry_points.command: open Finished Presentations/crm-three-scenarios.html; Space / ArrowRight = next step, ArrowLeft = previous slide, N = notes, Home / End
entry_points.what: Runs the deck: each key press reveals the next animation step or the next slide; N opens the provenance notes panel.

architecture.responsibility: Design rules for script -> HTML decks: colour psychology, typography maxima (h1 max 60px), safe zones, sequential animations, keyboard controls, mandatory lead-magnet CTA for YouTube decks. scripts/, style-references/ and Finished Presentations/ are its folders.

The only context boundary: the request verbatim (3 scenarios, 6-row gates table, stories and images), admissible sources with provenance tags, output conventions, and section 5 for the sequel request and its tracker source.

Text extracts of the owner's 2026 review deck and roadmap tracker, two CRM-health screenshots, and the 13-Oct remediation-plan CSV (22 task rows), copied beside the brief so locators stay repository-relative.
One JSON per source family (hs-logic, hubspot-ruler, deck-tracker, live-crm, pricing, remediation-plan) holding items, facts and gaps; every fact has a story_link and evidence.

15 built items ranked with exactly one verdict word each (keep, simplify, consolidate, pay_for), where each lives and what it is built on; cost-lines.md prices each scenario with provenance and a confidence tier.

The evidence graph: 282 nodes, 736 edges, 25 views. Narrative nodes sit at depths 1-3, evidence_fact nodes (183: 85 confirmed, 98 caveat) at depth 4; views are the planned slides with the node ids they cite.

Stdlib script: co-citation x folder-proximity scores, idempotent metagraph.md with wikilinks and Co-cited tables, and the grounded-path guard that fails the run. Canonical copy in the skill at .claude/skills/structured-citation-metagraph/scripts/citation_graph.py; this project copy differs only at line 137.

Stdlib script at .claude/skills/structured-citation-metagraph/scripts/deck_cites_check.py closing the plan-to-build gap: reads data-claim ids (HTML) or ^Cxxx^ / [Cxxx] (Markdown) from the built deck and checks them against the graph.

One row per claim id (id, kind, claim, used by, source, locator, quote) with a Verification header (counts, refuted ids with the verifier's corrected reading) and the list of unsupported, illustrative story elements.

27 self-contained slides, inline SVG metaphors, every number in an element with data-claim and data-source, per-slide .notes block with claim status / caveat / provenance, animation map keyed by data-view.
HTML -> pandoc Markdown -> pptx. SlideConverter maps deck classes to blocks, chunk() splits by line budget, notes become speaker notes; render_figures.js supplies the PNG figures and manifest.

Skill folder at .claude/skills/structured-citation-metagraph/: SKILL.md (roles 0-6, invariants, pitfalls), references/ (schemas, brief template, method.md, the workflow script that ran the case), scripts/ (both guards), evals/ (3 prompts).

data_flow: 0. Scout and brief: the orchestrator lists the repos, extracts uploaded deck and tracker text, pulls screenshots, probes the read-only HubSpot connector once, then writes brief.md with the request verbatim, tagged admissible sources and output conventions.

1. Explore: five explorers run in parallel, one per source family (Hs-Logic repo, HubSpot-Ruler repo, deck + tracker, live CRM via read-only HubSQL, public pricing), each returning items / facts / gaps validated by INVENTORY_SCHEMA and written to an explore-*.json file. Worked case: 63 items, 135 facts, 55 gaps.

2. Rank: one health-check agent reads all explorer files and writes implementation-health-check.md (15 ranked items, one verdict word each) and cost-lines.md (per-scenario cost lines with confidence).

3. Metagraph: one agent builds metagraph.json (stories and scenarios at depth 1, images and gate cells at 2, data problems / examples / projects / cost lines at 3, evidence facts at 4), plans the views, writes evidence-ledger.md, then runs citation_graph.py until the guard passes.

4. Verify: claims are sliced into batches of 8; each batch gets two verifiers in parallel (source fidelity, numeric and logical consistency). Any refuted verdict wins, else any caveat, else confirmed. First pass: 69 confirmed, 83 caveat, 4 refuted (C058, C126, C128, C146).
5. Maintain: a maintainer agent writes caveats into attrs.caveat, removes refuted claims from view cites, adds the Verification section to the ledger and re-runs the guard to exit 0.

6. Present: one agent writes the spoken script (scripts/crm-three-scenarios-script.txt) then the HTML deck from the graph: views become slides, numbers carry data-claim, caveated wording is the wording shown, deviations from the view plan are logged in notes.

7. QA loop (max 3 rounds): render, fact-drift and design-rule checks run in parallel; a fixer agent repairs blocker / major issues between rounds. Worked case: round 1 had 18 issues (5 blocking, all layout), round 2 had 16 minor.
8. Hygiene and commit: scratch paths rewritten to repository-relative, forbidden tokens scrubbed, metagraph.md regenerated, guard and idempotency re-checked.

9. PPTX: render_figures.js rasterises SVGs to PNG + manifest.json; build_pptx.py writes crm-three-scenarios.md; pandoc with reference.pptx produces the pptx (27 HTML slides -> 90 pptx slides after the sequel).

10. Sequel (2026-10-12): remediation tracker CSV added as a source, claims C158-C171 verified (1 confirmed, 13 caveat), side findings filed as C172-C187, node types plan / plan_layer and views V23-V25 added, three slides inserted before the appendices, pptx regenerated.

key_functions.name: folder_proximity
key_functions.does: Returns 1 / 2 ** (max_depth - shared_ancestor_depth): the hierarchy bonus that halves for every level two nodes do not share. It only breaks ties between equally co-cited nodes.
key_functions.input_example: max_depth = 4; dp_modelling and its own child fact C067 (shared ancestor depth 3)
key_functions.expected_output: 0.5 (documented dry-run row: prox 0.500). Sibling scenarios s1_diy / s2_partner share nothing: 1/2**4 = 0.0625, printed as 0.062.

key_functions.name: score_pairs
key_functions.signature: def score_pairs(nodes, views, co, chains, max_depth, w_co, w_prox)
key_functions.does: combined = w_co * co_citation + w_prox * folder_proximity, computed only for pairs that share at least one view (not all N^2 pairs). Default weights 0.7 / 0.3.
key_functions.expected_output: 0.7*2 + 0.3*0.5 = 1.550 (method.md table); s2_partner <-> s1_diy with co = 3 gives 2.119

key_functions.name: build_co_citation_matrix
key_functions.does: For each view, de-duplicates and sorts its cites and adds 1 to both (a, b) and (b, a) for every pair: co-citation = number of views (slides) citing both nodes.
key_functions.expected_output: co[('A','B')] == 2, co[('A','C')] == 1, symmetric entries equal (by reading the loop)

key_functions.name: grounded_ok
key_functions.does: Returns a memoised predicate: a node is grounded if it is an evidence_fact with at least one evidence entry holding source AND locator AND quote, or if a grounded_in edge leads (transitively, cycle-safe) to such a fact. Unknown ids are not grounded.
key_functions.input_example: an evidence_fact whose evidence has source and locator but an empty quote

key_functions.name: guard
key_functions.does: Lists (view id, title, bad ids) for every view citing an ungrounded node. main() prints 'PRESENTATION-LAYER GUARD FAILED' on stderr and exits 2 when the list is non-empty, else prints 'guard OK'.
key_functions.expected_output: On success: guard OK: every cited node in 25 views is grounded (format string at line 223, 25 views in the committed graph)

key_functions.name: render_md
key_functions.signature: def render_md(g, nodes, edges, views, scores, top_n, w_co, w_prox)
key_functions.does: Builds metagraph.md: a Views list, then one section per node grouped by type with attributes, an Edges list as [[wikilinks]] and a Co-cited table of the top-N scores. The file is replaced on every run, never appended.

key_functions.name: deck_cites_check (script body)
key_functions.does: At .claude/skills/structured-citation-metagraph/scripts/deck_cites_check.py:33. Extracts data-claim="Cxxx" ids (falls back to ^Cxxx^ / [Cxxx] only when no HTML attribute matched), reports unknown, not-an-evidence-fact, refuted and unplanned ids plus a caveat roll-call. Exit 1 on unknown / non-fact / refuted; --strict also on unplanned.
key_functions.expected_output: Worked case before the sequel (method.md): 153 distinct ids shown, all planned, none refuted or unknown, 83 caveated

key_functions.name: Verdict merge (workflow)
key_functions.does: workflow-crm-three-scenarios.js:289-294 in the skill's references/. Merges the two lenses per claim: refuted if any verdict is refuted, else caveat if any is caveat, else confirmed if at least one verdict exists, else unverified. Only non-confirmed entries go to the maintainer agent.
key_functions.input_example: source lens: confirmed; numeric lens: caveat

key_functions.name: Verify fan-out (workflow)
key_functions.does: workflow-crm-three-scenarios.js:263-284 in the skill's references/. Slices claims into batches of BATCH = 8 and runs every batch under both lenses in parallel with VERDICT_SCHEMA; the claim batch travels inline in the prompt (about 5 KB).

key_functions.name: QA loop (workflow)
key_functions.does: workflow-crm-three-scenarios.js:398 in the skill's references/. Runs render, facts and design QA agents in parallel; passes when no blocker / major issue remains, otherwise a fixer agent repairs the deck (and script / ledger for factual issues) and the loop repeats, up to 3 rounds.

key_functions.name: SlideConverter.visit
key_functions.does: Maps the deck's HTML vocabulary to Block objects: h1 -> slide title, svg -> image from the figure manifest, .tiles and .bars -> bullet lists, .chips -> one line, table.gates -> one table per scenario, .notes skipped (emitted later as speaker notes).

key_functions.name: chunk
key_functions.does: Groups blocks into pptx slides: a picture is alone on its slide and its caption opens the next text slide; a table is alone on its slide; text slides stay within LINES_PLAIN (11) estimated lines; a heading never ends a slide.
key_functions.expected_output: Deck level: 24 HTML slides became 74 pptx slides (method.md); 27 became 90 after the sequel (89 '## ' slides in the Markdown plus the YAML title slide)

key_functions.name: build_markdown
key_functions.does: Loads figures/manifest.json, parses every section.slide with lxml, emits a YAML title block from slide 1, then one '## ' slide per chunk titled '... (k/n)'; provenance notes go on the first pptx slide of each HTML slide. Returns (markdown, pptx slide count, HTML slide count).

key_functions.name: nextAction / goToSlide (deck JS)
key_functions.does: If the current slide still has animation steps in slideAnimations[slide.dataset.view], reveals the next selector group by adding .animate-in; otherwise moves to the next slide. goToSlide resets steps and auto-reveals step 0 after 80 ms.

infra.detail: No server, CI, Docker or cloud resources. Deliverables are static files committed to the repo: a self-contained HTML deck (system fonts, inline SVG, no external assets) and a .pptx in Finished Presentations/. Work lives on branch claude/affectionate-brahmagupta-r8n7t5 of a public fork.

Claude Code workflow script (skill references/workflow-crm-three-scenarios.js) with six phases (Explore, Health check, Metagraph, Verify, Presentation, QA) using phase(), log(), agent() with JSON schemas, and parallel(). Paths are placeholders (<work-dir>, <repo>, <checkout>). Worked-case cost: 56 agents, 1,208 tool calls, 6.98 M tokens, 254.7 min wall clock; verification took 53 % of tokens.

infra.topic: External sources used at run time
infra.detail: HubSpot MCP tools in read-only mode (query_crm_data HubSQL, search_properties, get_organization_details) against portal [id]; WebSearch / WebFetch for public pricing pages with as-of dates; sibling repositories Hs-Logic and HubSpot-Ruler read from disk.

Node with Playwright + Chromium (env var PLAYWRIGHT_MODULE points at the module when not resolvable), Python 3 with lxml, pandoc with --reference-doc reference.pptx (pandoc's own template with body 16 pt and titles 26 pt). QA used the pptx skill's validate.py, LibreOffice --convert-to pdf, pdftoppm contact sheets and markitdown.

Claude Code skill folder .claude/skills/structured-citation-metagraph/: SKILL.md (frontmatter name + trigger description), scripts/ (two stdlib Python guards), references/ (method, schemas, brief template, workflow) and evals/evals.json with three test prompts. Not yet run on a second project.

The render QA agent (workflow script, QA_CHECKS) opens the deck with Playwright at 1920x1080, 1440x900, 1366x768 and 375x667, steps through every slide and animation, and asserts no clipping, overflow or console errors (env var PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH locates Chromium). The deck exposes window.deckState() and window.goToSlide for this.

decisions.decision: Build a presentation layer, not a decision layer: show grounded truth against three scenarios and never recommend one.
decisions.why: The request says the citation algorithm keeps the context that governs the scenarios; a tight boundary between desired outcome and reality yields a presentation layer rather than a decision layer. Verdict words apply to built items, never to scenarios.
decisions.alternative_rejected: A persuasive pitch or a recommendation slide

decisions.decision: A view may cite a node only if it has a grounded_in path to an evidence fact carrying source, locator and quote; the script exits non-zero otherwise.
decisions.why: It is this gate, not the scoring, that keeps the deck honest: a story node with no grounded path cannot appear on a slide except as a labelled metaphor. A fact without the triple cannot be verified by anyone later.
decisions.alternative_rejected: Trusting prose synthesis or relaxing the triple for 'obvious' facts

decisions.decision: Verify every claim before the deck is written, not after.
decisions.why: The presentation agent writes with caveated wording already decided, so QA only has layout to fix; verifying after writing makes every refutation a slide rewrite. In the run, no QA blocker was factual.
decisions.alternative_rejected: Write the deck first and fact-check it afterwards

decisions.decision: Two different verification lenses per batch (source fidelity, numeric and logical consistency) instead of N identical refuters.
decisions.why: The two lenses found different things: the four refutations were fabrications, and the 83 caveats re-scoped numbers (partial scan, subset denominator, as-of date) rather than rejecting them, which was the real return of 3.7 M tokens.
decisions.alternative_rejected: Several identical adversarial reviewers, or a single verifier

decisions.decision: Files are the bus between agents; schemas are the contract; the orchestrator reads only typed summaries and paths.
decisions.why: Each agent reads brief.md and writes its full output to a named file, so nothing of substance travels in a prompt except claim batches and verdicts. This kept the orchestrator's context a control loop: it counted 135 facts instead of reading them.
decisions.alternative_rejected: Passing raw material through prompts or the orchestrator's context

decisions.decision: Score neighbours as 0.7 x co-citation + 0.3 x folder proximity, with slides as views and the entity hierarchy as folders.
decisions.why: Reused unchanged from the owner's citation-algorithm plan. Proximity is small by design (halving per level) so it only breaks ties; the neighbourhood comes from where things were shown together, not from prose adjacency.
decisions.alternative_rejected: Prose adjacency or an equal-weight proximity term

decisions.decision: Keep refuted claims as nodes with status refuted and retire their ids, instead of deleting them.
decisions.why: In the worked case refuted claims were deleted; keeping them as negative evidence lets a deck say 'two pricing claims were refuted' with a citation, and a retired id can never be silently reused.
decisions.alternative_rejected: Delete the node, its edges and view cites (what the first pass did)

decisions.decision: Write the boundary brief inside the project folder with repository-relative locators from the first minute.
decisions.why: The first brief cited scratchpad paths, which leaked into 143 locators in the graph and 84 in the ledger and had to be rewritten by hand; scratch locators die when the session ends.
decisions.alternative_rejected: A brief and extracts kept in a session scratch directory

decisions.decision: Produce PowerPoint through an editable Markdown intermediate (HTML -> Markdown -> pandoc) with a 16 pt reference template, one picture or table per slide.
decisions.why: The HTML deck stays the source of truth; wording can be edited in Markdown and facts only in HTML + ledger. Pandoc's stock 24 pt body overflows dense slides, and its two-column and caption layouts overlap pictures and tables.
decisions.alternative_rejected: Direct pandoc defaults, or building the pptx by hand

decisions.decision: Skip the upstream lead-magnet CTA slide and close with 'a presentation, not a decision'; light neutral style.
decisions.why: The audience is executive stakeholders, not YouTube viewers, so the mandatory CTA rule of Claude.MD is deliberately overridden for this deck.
decisions.alternative_rejected: Following Claude.MD's mandatory final CTA slide

gotchas.issue: A pricing explorer read a vendor calculator's default slider value as a price tier.
gotchas.consequence: A fabricated price band would have sat on a cost slide (claim C128, refuted).
gotchas.fix_or_guard: Only the source-fidelity verifier caught it: it re-opens the URL and checks the quote says exactly this.

gotchas.issue: git log -8 truncated a ten-commit history and hid the first commit.
gotchas.consequence: A provenance claim was wrong (C058 refuted) and the only evidence for the 'understand tech is outsourced' example was missed until harvested by hand as C157.
gotchas.fix_or_guard: Log without a count limit when provenance is the question; give verifiers a side_findings channel.

gotchas.issue: The live HubSQL engine summed an id column when asked to COUNT it and silently dropped an association filter inside a GROUP BY.
gotchas.consequence: Counts from the live portal can be silently wrong.
gotchas.fix_or_guard: Keep only COUNT(*) results and record the quirk as a methodological fact (Appendix A of the deck).

gotchas.issue: Capped scans (10,000 records) produce floors, not counts.
gotchas.consequence: A partial figure presented as a total; most of the 83 caveats were this kind of scope conflation.
gotchas.fix_or_guard: The caveat is stored in attrs.caveat and must travel to the slide or its notes; deck_cites_check.py lists every caveated claim.

gotchas.issue: The two copies of citation_graph.py differ at line 137: the project copy hard-codes the node-type order (with plan, plan_layer); the skill copy reads meta.node_types.
gotchas.consequence: With the project copy, a node type missing from the hard-coded list gets no section in metagraph.md; the two files can drift further.
gotchas.fix_or_guard: Use the skill copy (.claude/skills/structured-citation-metagraph/scripts/citation_graph.py) and declare new node types in meta.node_types.

gotchas.issue: The bundled workflow script (skill references/workflow-crm-three-scenarios.js:28 and :301) still carries first-run behaviour: EVIDENCE requires only source and locator (not quote), and the maintainer prompt says refuted -> remove.
gotchas.consequence: Reusing it verbatim contradicts the skill's invariants (evidence triple, refuted nodes kept with status refuted).
gotchas.fix_or_guard: SKILL.md says to reuse its phase shape and rewrite its prompts; tighten the schema to require quote.

gotchas.issue: A dense HTML slide (300-460 words, notes hidden behind N) does not fit a linear medium.
gotchas.consequence: 24 HTML slides became 74 pptx slides, 27 became 90; views in the committed graph carry no budget.
gotchas.fix_or_guard: Plan each view with a budget per medium (words for HTML, lines for pptx) before writing; --budget tunes the pptx chunking.

gotchas.issue: build_pptx.py is specific to this deck: default paths, the YAML date '2026-10-01' and the class vocabulary (tiles, bars, gates, hcgrid) are hard-coded; a stale docstring mentions WORDS_PLAIN.
gotchas.consequence: Reusing it for another deck silently mis-dates the title slide and drops unknown layouts into generic paragraphs.
gotchas.fix_or_guard: Pass --deck / --out / --figures and edit line 416; re-run render_figures.js first because figures are matched by slide and svgIndex.

glossary.meaning: The deck's rule: show grounded truth against the options and offer no choice. Nothing shown is a recommendation.
{source, locator, quote}: the minimum every fact must carry to be shown; without all three the guard treats the node as ungrounded.
metagraph.json: nodes (story, image, data_problem, practical_example, scenario, gate_cell, project, cost_line, evidence_fact, plan, plan_layer), typed edges and views, with max_depth 4.
A planned slide: an id (V01...V25), a title and the list of node ids it cites. Co-citation is counted over views.
The id of an evidence_fact node, shown on the deck as data-claim="C067" and as a row in the evidence ledger. Retired ids (refuted) are never reused.
The edge type that links a narrative node to its evidence; a node is citable only if a grounded_in path reaches a fact with a full evidence triple.
Number of views (slides) that cite both of two nodes; weight 0.7 in the combined score.
1 / 2^(max_depth - shared ancestor depth) along the parent chain, which plays the role of vault folders; weight 0.3.
brief.md: the only context boundary. The user's stories are admissible as 'what was asked', never as truth.
The data-source label of a source family, e.g. tracker-210926, live-hubsql-2026-10-01, sealsq-property-set-2026-09-14, public-pricing-<url>, brief-2026-10-12.
Price / fact tiers carried verbatim on cost slides: official list, vendor list, partner range, secondary, order of magnitude, illustrative, tracker words, not priced.
Claim verdicts: confirmed, caveat, refuted (default refuted when unverifiable). Health-check verdicts about built items: keep, simplify, consolidate, pay_for.
The two verifier roles per batch of 8 claims: source fidelity (re-open the source) and numeric and logical consistency (recompute, catch scope conflation).
The user's 6 rows x 3 scenarios matrix (sampling probe, schema blueprint, rules to comply, declarative action layer, new cost lines, depends on) = 18 gate_cell nodes.
Label for story elements and metaphors (iceberg, Team A pitch, speedometer, messy landlord, Team B) that found no evidence; 18 such elements in the first pass.

directions: Run the skill on a second project (method.md says this is the next step) and execute the three prompts in evals/evals.json, since the skill has only its originating case.

Update the bundled workflow script to the skill's own rules: require quote in EVIDENCE, add side_findings to VERDICT_SCHEMA, keep refuted nodes, add kind / confidence to the explorer schema, and call deck_cites_check.py as a QA step.
Add a budget per medium to each view in metagraph.json (currently none) so dense slides are split at planning time instead of at pptx conversion.
Script the hygiene pass (path normalisation, forbidden-token and personal-data scrub, idempotent regeneration check) that the orchestrator did by hand.
Unify the two citation_graph.py copies and generalise build_pptx.py (date, paths, class map) so the 'pptx recovery pattern' works for any deck.
Reuse the claim-id + evidence-quote + guard pattern for other grounded outputs (documentation pages, flashcards): it is the same 'every statement cites a locator and a quote' contract.
coverage_notes: Read in full: the skill folder (SKILL.md, schemas, brief template, evals, method.md, both scripts), pptx/README.md, build_pptx.py, render_figures.js, the deck's script block, README.md; workflow script read for control flow, verify, QA and explorer prompts. brief.md sections 1, 2e, 2f, 3, 5 read. metagraph.json summarised by counting. Health check, cost lines, ledger read by headings and verification header; explore JSONs, sources/ extracts and metagraph.md not read (CRM detail and people). Nothing executed. CITATION NOTE: the validator cannot resolve paths starting with '.claude', so skill files are cited through identical project copies (citation_graph.py, method-structured-citation-metagraph.md) or through the method.md lines that describe them; the real skill path is given in the text.
